title: 难道…吗, 到底 and 究竟: asking with force
explain: 难道 … 吗 is a question that already has an answer in the speaker's mind. 难道 means 'could it be that …?' and shows surprise or doubt: 难道你不知道吗 'Do you really not know?'. It is not a real request for information.
到底 and 究竟 both mean 'on earth, exactly' in a question. They add force to the question and show you want a clear answer: 你到底想吃什么 'What on earth do you want to eat?'. 究竟 is a little more formal.
到底 also means 'in the end, after all' in a statement: 他到底还是来了 'He came after all'. Put 到底 and 究竟 before the verb or before the question word.

examples.zh: 难道你不知道吗？
examples.en: Do you really not know?

examples.zh: 难道他没有告诉你吗？
examples.en: Has he really not told you?

examples.zh: 你到底想吃什么？
examples.en: What on earth do you want to eat?

examples.zh: 你究竟去不去？
examples.en: Are you going or not, once and for all?

mistakes: 难道 … 吗 is not a plain question. Use it when you are surprised. For a real question, use 吗 alone.
Do not use 到底 in a yes/no question with 吗: 你到底去吗 is odd. Use a question word or A-not-A: 你到底去不去.

q.en: Do you really not like it?
q.explain: 难道 + statement + 吗.

q.en: What on earth do you want to eat?
q.explain: 到底 goes before the verb.

q.en: Are you going or not, once and for all?
q.explain: 究竟 adds force to the question.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: What on earth is this?
q.en: What on earth is this?
q.explain: 到底 comes before the verb 是.

q.en: Do you really not know?
q.explain: 难道 already adds force; do not add 到底.

title: 竟然, 原来 and 本来: surprise and discovery
explain: 竟然 'to one's surprise, actually' shows you did not expect what happened: 他竟然忘了自己的生日 'He actually forgot his own birthday'. It goes before the verb and comes with something the speaker finds hard to believe.
原来 'so it turns out' marks a discovery: you have just found out the truth. 原来你在这儿 'So you are here!'; 原来他是老师 'So he is a teacher'. It usually starts the sentence.
本来 'originally, in the first place' tells what was planned or true before something changed: 我本来想去，可是下雨了 'I originally wanted to go, but it rained'.

examples.zh: 他竟然忘了自己的生日。
examples.en: He actually forgot his own birthday.

examples.zh: 这么简单的题，他竟然做错了。
examples.en: He actually got such an easy question wrong.

examples.zh: 原来你在这儿，我找了你很久。
examples.en: So you are here! I looked for you for a long time.

examples.zh: 我本来想去，可是下雨了。
examples.en: I originally wanted to go, but it rained.

mistakes: 竟然 is for surprise, not for a plain fact. If the thing is not surprising, do not use it.
原来 is about finding out. Do not use it for something you already knew.

q.en: He actually forgot my name.
q.explain: 竟然 goes before the verb.

q.zh: 我本来想去，可是太累了。
q.en: I originally wanted to go, but I was too tired.
q.explain: 本来 tells the first plan.

q.zh: 原来他是我们的新老师。
q.en: So he is our new teacher.
q.explain: 原来 marks a discovery.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: She actually did not come?
q.en: She actually did not come.
q.explain: 竟然 comes before 没有.

q.en: He actually does not know about this.
q.wrong: 他竟然却不知道这件事。
q.explain: Do not add 却 after 竟然.

title: 确实, 实在, 完全 and 十分: really and completely
explain: 确实 'really, indeed' confirms that something is true: 这个办法确实很好 'This way really is good'. 实在 'truly' stresses a feeling or a judgement and is often used with 太 or 不: 我实在太累了 'I am truly too tired'.
完全 'completely, entirely' goes before a verb or adjective: 我完全同意 'I completely agree'. With 不 it means 'not at all': 我完全不知道 'I have no idea at all'.
十分 'very, fully' is like 非常 or 很 but a little more formal. It goes before an adjective or a feeling: 他十分高兴 'He is very happy'.

examples.zh: 这个办法确实很好。
examples.en: This way really is good.

examples.zh: 我实在太累了，想休息一下。
examples.en: I am really too tired and want to rest a bit.

examples.zh: 我完全同意你说的。
examples.en: I completely agree with what you say.

examples.zh: 他对这个工作十分满意。
examples.en: He is very satisfied with this job.

mistakes: 完全 and 十分 go before the verb or adjective, not after it. 我同意完全 is wrong.
确实 confirms what is true. Do not use it to ask a question; for "is it really so?" use 真的吗.

q.zh: 这个电影确实很有意思。
q.en: This film really is interesting.
q.explain: 确实 goes before the adjective.

q.en: I completely agree with your view.
q.explain: 完全 goes before the verb.

q.en: I am really too tired; I do not want to go.
q.explain: 实在 stresses how strongly you feel.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: He is very happy?
q.en: He is very happy.
q.explain: 十分 goes before the adjective.

q.en: I know nothing at all about this.
q.wrong: 我完全不是知道这件事。
q.explain: 完全不 + verb; do not add 是.

title: 从来, 并 and 往往: never, not at all, tends to
explain: 从来 + 不 / 没 means 'never, at no time': 我从来不喝酒 'I never drink alcohol'; 他从来没去过那个地方 'He has never been to that place'. 从来不 is a habit or a rule; 从来没 + verb + 过 is experience up to now. 从来 is normally used with a negative.
并 + 不 / 没 'not at all, actually not' corrects a wrong idea: 这个菜并不贵 'This dish is not expensive at all'; 他并没有生气 'He did not actually get angry'. 并 only goes with a negative.

往往 'often, tends to' describes what usually happens in the same situation. It is a pattern, not one event: 周末他往往在家休息 'At the weekend he tends to rest at home'. Use 常常 for plain frequency and 往往 for a general rule.

examples.zh: 我从来不喝酒。
examples.en: I never drink alcohol.

examples.zh: 他从来没去过那个地方。
examples.en: He has never been to that place.

examples.zh: 这个菜并不贵，只是有点儿辣。
examples.en: This dish is not expensive at all; it is just a little spicy.

examples.zh: 周末他往往在家休息。
examples.en: At the weekend he tends to rest at home.

mistakes: 从来 and 并 need a negative. 我从来去过 is wrong; say 我从来没去过.
往往 describes what usually happens. It is not used for the future or for a command: 明天他往往来 is wrong.

q.en: I never eat breakfast.
q.explain: 从来 + 不 + verb.

q.en: He has never been here.
q.explain: 从来没 + verb + 过.

q.en: This piece of clothing is not expensive at all.
q.explain: 并 goes with 不 or 没.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: Old people tend to get up early?
options: 老人往往明天起得很早。
q.en: Old people tend to get up early.
q.explain: 往往 describes a general pattern, not tomorrow.

q.en: He did not actually get angry.
q.explain: Do not add 也 after 并.

title: 偶尔, 不断, 老是 and 差点儿: how often, and nearly
explain: 偶尔 'now and then, occasionally' is for something that happens rarely: 我偶尔去看电影 'I go to the cinema now and then'. 不断 'again and again, without a break' says something goes on and on: 他不断地练习 'He keeps practising'. 老是 'always, all the time' is spoken and often complains: 他老是迟到 'He is always late'.
不断 is often followed by 地 and a verb. 老是 is close to 总是 (HSK 3), but 老是 usually shows that the speaker is not happy about it.
差点儿 'almost, nearly' says that something nearly happened, but did not: 我昨天差点儿迟到 'I was almost late yesterday' (and I was not). It goes right before the verb: 他差点儿忘了 'He almost forgot'.

examples.zh: 我偶尔去看电影。
examples.en: I go to the cinema now and then.

examples.zh: 他不断地练习，所以汉语越来越好。
examples.en: He keeps practising, so his Chinese is getting better and better.

examples.zh: 他老是迟到，老师很不高兴。
examples.en: He is always late, and the teacher is very unhappy.

examples.zh: 我昨天差点儿迟到。
examples.en: I was almost late yesterday.

mistakes: 偶尔 means rarely, so do not use it with a fixed number of times: 我偶尔去三次 is wrong.
差点儿 describes something that did not happen. 我差点儿迟到 means you were not late.

q.en: I go running in the park now and then.
q.explain: 偶尔 goes before the verb.

q.en: He always forgets to bring his phone.
q.explain: 老是 = all the time, and the speaker is not happy.

q.en: He keeps practising writing characters.
q.explain: 不断地 + verb = again and again.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: I was almost late yesterday?
q.en: I was almost late yesterday.
q.explain: 差点儿 means it nearly happened.

q.en: He almost forgot.
q.explain: 差点儿 goes straight before the verb.

title: 至少, 左右, 大约, 尤其 and 其中: amounts and focus
explain: 至少 'at least' goes before an amount: 我每天至少睡七个小时 'I sleep at least seven hours every day'. 左右 'about' goes after a number: 他三十岁左右 'He is about thirty'. 大约 'about, roughly' goes before it: 大约三十个人 'about thirty people'. Do not use both in one phrase.
尤其 'especially' picks out the most important case: 我喜欢水果，尤其是苹果 'I like fruit, especially apples'. 尤其 is often followed by 是 and can point at a thing, a time or a quality.
其中 'among them, of which' points back to a group you have just named: 这里有十个人，其中三个是老师 'There are ten people here, and three of them are teachers'.

examples.zh: 我每天至少睡七个小时。
examples.en: I sleep at least seven hours every day.

examples.zh: 他三十岁左右，是一个医生。
examples.en: He is about thirty and is a doctor.

examples.zh: 我喜欢水果，尤其是苹果。
examples.en: I like fruit, especially apples.

examples.zh: 这里有十个人，其中三个是老师。
examples.en: There are ten people here, and three of them are teachers.

mistakes: 左右 goes after the number, 大约 before it. 左右三十 is wrong. Do not use 大约 and 左右 together.
其中 points back to a group you have already named. Do not use it at the start of a text.

q.en: He drinks at least three glasses of water every day.
q.explain: 至少 goes before the amount.

q.zh: 这个小城市大约有五千人。
q.en: This small city has about 5,000 people.
q.explain: 大约 goes before the number.

q.zh: 我喜欢运动，尤其是游泳。
q.en: I like sports, especially swimming.
q.explain: 尤其是 picks out the main case.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: He is about twenty years old?
q.en: He is about twenty years old.
q.explain: 左右 goes after the number.

q.zh: 我们有五个人，其中两个是老师。
q.en: We have five people, and two of them are teachers.
q.wrong: 我们有五个人，在其中两个是老师。
q.explain: 其中 stands alone; do not put 在 before it.

title: 也许, 恐怕, 估计, 肯定, 千万 and 无法: guessing and warning
explain: 也许 'maybe, perhaps' and 估计 'I guess' show that you are not sure: 他也许在家 'He may be at home'; 我估计明天会下雨 'I guess it will rain tomorrow'. 恐怕 'I am afraid that' is a polite way to give bad news or a doubt: 恐怕我不能去 'I am afraid I cannot go'. 肯定 'definitely, certainly' shows you are sure: 他肯定知道 'He definitely knows'.
千万 'be sure to, on no account' gives a strong warning, mostly in commands: 千万别忘了 'Be sure not to forget'; 路上千万小心 'Be very careful on the road'.
无法 'unable to, there is no way to' is the formal form of 不能: 我无法回答这个问题 'I cannot answer this question'. It is followed by a verb and shows that there really is no way.

examples.zh: 他也许在家，给他打个电话吧。
examples.en: Perhaps he is at home; give him a call.

examples.zh: 我估计明天会下雨。
examples.en: I guess it will rain tomorrow.

examples.zh: 恐怕我不能去，对不起。
examples.en: I am afraid I cannot go; sorry.

examples.zh: 路上千万小心。
examples.en: Be very careful on the road.

mistakes: 恐怕 gives bad news or a doubt. Do not use it for good news: 恐怕你会赢 sounds odd.
千万 is for warnings and commands, not for the past: 昨天我千万去了 is wrong.

q.en: He definitely knows about this.
q.explain: 肯定 shows you are sure.

q.en: Perhaps it will rain today.
q.explain: 也许 = perhaps.

q.en: I am afraid he cannot come today.
q.explain: 恐怕 gives a polite doubt or bad news.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: Be sure not to forget?
q.en: Be sure not to forget.
q.explain: 千万 goes with 别 or 不要 in a warning.

q.en: I cannot answer this question.
q.wrong: 我无法能回答这个问题。
q.explain: 无法 already means "cannot"; do not add 能.

title: 仍然, 重新, 继续 and 最终: still, again, go on, in the end
explain: 仍然 and 仍 'still, yet' say that a situation has not changed: 他仍然住在那里 'He still lives there'. They are more formal than 还 and 还是 and go before the verb or the adjective.

重新 'anew, from the start' means to do something again in a new way: 我想重新开始 'I want to start again'. Unlike 再 or 又, 重新 means starting over. 继续 'to continue' picks up what was going on: 请继续说 'Please go on talking'.

最终 'in the end' tells the result after a long process: 他努力学习，最终通过了考试 'He studied hard and in the end passed the exam'. It is more formal than 最后 and is about the result, not about the last item in a list.

examples.zh: 他仍然住在那个小城市里。
examples.en: He still lives in that small city.

examples.zh: 我想重新开始学习汉语。
examples.en: I want to start learning Chinese again from the beginning.

examples.zh: 请继续说，我在听。
examples.en: Please go on; I am listening.

examples.zh: 他努力学习，最终通过了考试。
examples.en: He studied hard and in the end passed the exam.

mistakes: 仍然 is for a situation that has stayed the same. For something that happens once more use 又 or 再.
重新 means starting over. For simply "one more time" use 再: 再说一遍.

q.en: He still works at the school.
q.explain: 仍然 goes before the verb.

q.en: Let us continue the lesson.
q.explain: 继续 = go on.

q.zh: 这个作业我想重新做一次。
q.en: I want to do this homework again from the start.
q.explain: 重新 = from the start.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: He still has not come?
q.en: He still has not come.
q.explain: 仍然 says nothing has changed.

q.en: In the end he passed the exam.
q.wrong: 他最终最后通过了考试。
q.explain: Use 最终 or 最后, not both.

title: 稍微, 有点儿, 多么, 却 and 倒: a little, how, but
explain: 稍微 'slightly, a little' is for a small amount or change: 请稍微等一下 'Please wait a moment'; 今天稍微热了一点儿 'Today is a little hotter'. It usually goes with 一点儿 or 一下. 有点儿 'a bit' is also small, but the speaker finds it too much: 这个有点儿贵 'This is a bit dear'.
多么 'how …!' is used in exclamations about a quality: 她唱得多么好啊 'How well she sings!'. It is followed by an adjective, and 啊 adds feeling.

却 and 倒 both turn the meaning against what you would expect, and both go before the verb. 却 'but, yet': 他很聪明，却不努力 'He is clever, but he does not work hard'. 倒 'actually, contrary to expectation': 这个菜看起来一般，吃起来倒很好吃 'This dish looks ordinary, but it tastes very good'.

examples.zh: 请稍微等一下，我马上来。
examples.en: Please wait a moment; I will come right away.

examples.zh: 这件衣服有点儿贵。
examples.en: This piece of clothing is a bit dear.

examples.zh: 她唱得多么好啊！
examples.en: How well she sings!

examples.zh: 他很聪明，却不努力。
examples.en: He is clever, but he does not work hard.

mistakes: 有点儿 often means "a bit too much", so it goes with unwelcome words: 有点儿贵, 有点儿累. It is not used with 很.
却 goes before the verb, not at the start of the sentence: 却他不努力 is wrong.

q.en: Please wait a moment.
q.explain: 稍微 goes before the verb.

q.en: This room is a bit small.
q.explain: 有点儿 + unwelcome adjective.

q.en: How pretty she is!
q.explain: 多么 + adjective + 啊 makes an exclamation.

q.prompt: Which sentence says: He is clever, but he does not work hard?
q.en: He is clever, but he does not work hard.
q.explain: 却 goes before the verb.

q.en: This dish is a bit spicy.
q.explain: 有点儿 is not used with 很.
